summary: Caisson light in Chesapeake Bay, Talbot County, Maryland: the third light here, lit in 1882 after ice destroyed its screw-pile predecessor in 1881. Sold to a private buyer in 2008.

light.characteristic: Fl W 6s, red sector 159°-262° (2009 Light List, per LighthouseFriends)

lens.note: replaced 1977 by a 250 mm plastic lens

structures.note: Cast-iron tower on a 30 ft (9 m) caisson per LighthouseFriends and the Chesapeake Chapter; the nomination calls the caisson steel and the tower 54 ft high.

access.note: Buyer named in 2008 as AFB, Inc.; current owner not confirmed. The GSA bid notice called the lighthouse physically inaccessible.

visit.note: Not open. Do not land or climb.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1838 wooden first light and the 1882 cast-iron caisson are different structures; the nomination and the Chesapeake Chapter date them separately, so the conflicting first years belong to different towers.

The nomination describes a steel caisson with a steel shell over brick; LighthouseFriends and the Chesapeake Chapter describe a cast-iron caisson. The story states the disagreement and does not choose.

notes_for_editor: Revision pass on the earlier draft. Changes: the 'winter thaw' is now cited to the Chesapeake Chapter page (it is not in the Board report); the lens, oil and library recovery is attributed to LighthouseFriends only (the Board passage read does not give it); the Snow Hill item is the only source naming Paw-Paw Cove; LighthouseFriends quotations cut to short phrases (copyrighted-source limit). Open conflicts stated in the story: screw-pile completion (late 1865 Chesapeake Chapter vs April 1866 appropriation and 1866 completion per LighthouseFriends and NRHP); screw-pile position (NRHP: about one mile east of the first site; LighthouseFriends: four miles off Tilghman Island); caisson dates (LighthouseFriends puts the tender's arrival at 28 Aug 1882 but the first lighting at 1 Feb 1882, which is earlier); tower height (NRHP 54 ft tower vs Chesapeake Chapter and LighthouseFriends 37 ft tower, light 54 ft above water); fog-bell room year (LighthouseFriends 1890; the 1891-92 Board passage gives no year); island acreage (700 in 1675 per NRHP; about 900 per LighthouseFriends and the Chapter); Board 1893 passage: the corpus page search labels scan 660 as 1893 and the grep labels it 1894; cited as the 1893-94 volume, scan p. 660, printed page not confirmed (corpus flags it with a question mark); check the page image before citing a printed page. Name variants: roster Christopher C. Butler vs LighthouseFriends Columbus Butler (1880-1890); Commissioner and Bulletin print Jesse M. W. Shockley (roster: Jesse M. Shockley); roster Benjamin Horney and Benjamin Harney for 1838 left as printed, not linked. Not used: a Bulletin 1918-23 index entry for 'William J. Thomas, keeper Sharps Island' (boat tow, index p. 180) is not on the roster and was not verified. The USCG Historian's page for Sharps Island was not readable through the archive (the capture returned a wrapper page), so no USCG text is used. Current status after 2010 is not confirmed by any source read; the 2008 buyer is named as a company as LighthouseFriends names it. The 1881 Maryland newspaper search on Chronicling America timed out; only the Snow Hill item (12 Mar 1881) was read. Roster is copied from the USLHS place record and not checked against NARA registers. The Bulletin page numbers are PDF pages from the corpus index. Fact-check 2026-10-22 (second pass): the caisson material is now stated as a disagreement (the nomination says steel; LighthouseFriends and the Chesapeake Chapter say cast iron). The 1893 Board passage is confirmed on printed p. 255 (the OCR page header reads 255); it recalls the February 1881 wreck as an example of heroism, so the story treats it as a retrospective account in the fiscal 1893 report. The 1893 keepers' passage also says the lens, pedestal, oil and library were saved, so the story cites it for the salvage as well as LighthouseFriends. The 1901 scaffold sentence now cites only the 1901 Board report (scan 148, confirmed; the 1891-92 and 1899 citations removed). The 1899 entry (scan 142) is confirmed. The Snow Hill item (12 March 1881, a paragraph headed 'condensed from' other papers) reads 'drifted ashore od Paw-Paw Core' in the OCR; the story gives only 'Paw-Paw' until the page image is checked, since 'Core' is probably 'Cove'. The Commissioner FY1921 and FY1922 entries (scan 665 and 753) are confirmed; the Bulletin 1921 uses 'J esse M. W. Sh ockley' in spaced OCR, so the full name is attributed to the Commissioner only. The Davis obituary (Bulletin 1926 p. 24) is confirmed. The 1928 Bulletin OCR is garbled ('brol{e dowu'), read as 'broke down'. The Lady Baltimore is described as a hydroairplane per LighthouseFriends; the Commissioner calls it a hydroplane. Current ownership is unconfirmed after 2008 and the record says so. The footnoted accessed dates (2026-10-23) post-date the 2026-10-22 check date and should be reconciled.
